title: Group Join with GroupJoin
description: Learn to perform left outer joins using the GroupJoin operator.

data.text: The `GroupJoin` operator joins two sequences based on keys and groups the results. It is equivalent to a **left outer join** in SQL.
`GroupJoin` requires the same parameters as `Join`. The key difference is that the result selector receives an `IEnumerable<TInner>` for the grouped inner sequence:

data.title: Left Outer Join Behavior
data.text: GroupJoin includes all elements from the outer sequence, even if there are no matches in the inner sequence. The inner collection will be empty for unmatched outer elements.
In query syntax, use the `into` keyword to create the grouped collection:

terms.definition: Inner join - returns only elements with matches in both sequences.
Left outer join - returns all outer elements with grouped inner matches.
In query syntax, creates the grouped collection for GroupJoin.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: GroupJoin performs a left outer join
All elements from the outer sequence are included
Inner elements are grouped into a collection
